rv.q: The Doctor is also an involving, stimulating, moving, handsomely staged and exquisitely acted night at the theatre.

An Icke production always involves an expansion of the mental horizons.
Icke's rigorous, visceral rethink...is a vital and immensely timely addition to the West End.
And in its stimulating experimentalism, it’s just what the doctor ordered to help resuscitate the cerebral life of our post-viral, musically bloated West End.
Full of smouldering frustration and just-visible terror, Stevenson's masterful central performance does a lot of heavy lifting here.

Impeccably executed stagecraft, inspired writing, and a terrific central performance fuse into a remarkable and revelatory piece of theatre.

This is a production that holds the attention drawing fine performances from the whole cast with Juliet Stevenson its vibrant centre.

Deep, thoughtful and intense, there’s sometimes so much shouting going on that one wonders if this is a play or a soap opera.

cn.t: Icke's provocative reworking of Schnitzler's 1912 play wins strong praise for its intellectual rigor and searing examination of identity politics, anchored by Stevenson's stunning performance, though some find it static and abrasive.
